put.summary: Link a site to a GitHub repository by hand (or change the link)
put.description: Saves the link in the settings file, replacing an earlier manual link of the site, and answers like GET /api/sites/{domain}. Refused when the site is Git-connected in Hostinger (SITE_GIT_CONNECTED): that connection always wins. Hostinger is asked afresh for this, so when Hostinger cannot be asked nothing is saved and the usual HOSTINGER_* problem is answered. GitHub is not needed: a repository that does not exist is saved and comes back with a `repoWarning`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The site's domain, e.g. example.com (case does not matter)

400.description: code INVALID_REPOSITORY: repoFullName is missing or not owner/name

404.description: code SITE_NOT_FOUND: Hostinger has no website with this domain

409.description: code SITE_GIT_CONNECTED: the site is Git-connected in Hostinger, a manual link cannot be set; code HOSTINGER_NOT_CONNECTED: no Hostinger token saved; code HOSTINGER_TOKEN_REJECTED: Hostinger rejected the saved token

429.description: code HOSTINGER_RATE_LIMITED: Hostinger's rate limit is reached

500.description: code SETTINGS_UNAVAILABLE: the settings file could not be written

502.description: code HOSTINGER_UNAVAILABLE: Hostinger could not be reached, timed out, failed or answered unexpectedly

delete.description: Does nothing when the site has no manual link. Needs neither Hostinger nor GitHub. A Hostinger Git connection is not touched (change that in hPanel).

put.summary: Check a Hostinger API token with Hostinger, then save it
put.description: Replaces any saved token, but only if Hostinger accepts the new one. On any error nothing is saved and an earlier token stays as it was.

200.description: Hostinger accepted the token; it is saved (state CONNECTED)

400.description: The token is missing, blank or too long

422.description: Hostinger rejected the token (HTTP 401/403); not saved

429.description: Hostinger's rate limit is reached; not saved, try again later

502.description: Hostinger could not be reached or answered with an error; not saved

delete.summary: Remove the Hostinger token from Dockline
delete.description: Afterwards HOSTINGER is NOT_CONNECTED. Does nothing when no token is saved.

get.summary: One site and its linked GitHub repository
get.description: The repository comes from Hostinger's Git settings of the site (source HOSTINGER; this always wins, and a saved manual link is then not shown), else from the manual link (MANUAL), else there is none (NONE). The repository is checked with GitHub: one that is missing or not accessible gives a `repoWarning`, not an error. A source that cannot be asked does not fail the request: it adds an entry to `problems` (codes HOSTINGER_NOT_CONNECTED, HOSTINGER_TOKEN_REJECTED, HOSTINGER_RATE_LIMITED, HOSTINGER_UNAVAILABLE, GITHUB_NOT_CONNECTED, GITHUB_TOKEN_REJECTED, GITHUB_RATE_LIMITED, GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE). Without Hostinger (`hostingerChecked` false) the answer comes from the saved manual links alone; without GitHub the repository is shown unchecked. Hostinger's answer about the site is kept for five minutes.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: The site's domain, e.g. example.com (case does not matter)

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: True asks Hostinger again about this site's Git connection instead of using the answer saved in the last five minutes (one or two Hostinger requests)

404.description: code SITE_NOT_FOUND: Hostinger has no website with this domain

get.summary: The linked repository of every site, for the Sites list
get.description: Always answers 200. For each Hostinger website with a domain: the repository from Hostinger's Git settings (source HOSTINGER), else the manual link (MANUAL), else NONE. GitHub is not asked. Asking Hostinger costs one or two requests per site, so the answers are kept for five minutes, and one call asks about at most 40 requests' worth of sites: with more sites than that, the rest have `hostingerChecked` false (`complete` false) and are filled in by a later call. When Hostinger cannot be asked (not connected, rejected token, rate limit, outage) `problems` holds one HOSTINGER entry with the usual HOSTINGER_* code, and the saved manual links are still returned.

get.summary: The latest deploy of every site, for the Sites list
get.description: For each Hostinger website with a domain: the status, time and commit of its latest deploy. Deploy information exists only for Node.js websites (`website_type` nodejs), from Hostinger's build history (source HOSTINGER); every other website, and a Node.js website that was never built, has status NONE and source NONE, and costs no Hostinger request. A Node.js website costs one Hostinger request (two with more than 100 builds). The answers are kept for 20 seconds, so calling this every 30 seconds shows changes; `refresh=true` asks Hostinger again at once. The website list itself is the copy saved in the last 60 s. A failure for one site does not fail the request: that site has status UNKNOWN and one entry in its `problems` (codes HOSTINGER_UNAVAILABLE, HOSTINGER_RATE_LIMITED with `retryAfterSeconds`, HOSTINGER_TOKEN_REJECTED, HOSTINGER_NOT_CONNECTED), and the failure is written to the Log section. After a rate limit or a rejected token Hostinger is not asked about the remaining sites in that call: they are answered from the saved answers, or get the same problem. Only when the website list itself cannot be read is the answer a problem response, with the same codes as GET /api/hostinger/sites.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: True skips the deploy answers saved in the last 20 seconds and asks Hostinger again about every Node.js website (counts towards the 50 requests per minute)

200.description: The latest deploy per site, sorted by domain

409.description: code HOSTINGER_NOT_CONNECTED: no Hostinger token saved; code HOSTINGER_TOKEN_REJECTED: Hostinger rejected the saved token (revoked or expired), replace it

429.description: code HOSTINGER_RATE_LIMITED: Hostinger's rate limit is reached

get.summary: Everything the Overview page shows, in one call
get.description: Always answers 200. Built from the same data as the other views, with their saved copies and the Hostinger cap of 50 requests per minute: the website list and the domains (copies up to 60 s old), the deploys (20 s), the sites' Git connections (five minutes, as in GET /api/sites/links) and the GitHub repositories (asked on every call, as in GET /api/github/repositories). Problems are failed latest deploys, expired domains and domains expiring within 30 days, broken site–repo links (a linked repository that is not among the user's GitHub repositories; not checked when the repository list is truncated) and sources that are not connected or not working fully. A source that cannot be asked does not fail the request: each part that needs it has an entry in its `errors` (codes HOSTINGER_NOT_CONNECTED, HOSTINGER_TOKEN_REJECTED, HOSTINGER_RATE_LIMITED, HOSTINGER_UNAVAILABLE, GITHUB_NOT_CONNECTED, GITHUB_TOKEN_REJECTED, GITHUB_RATE_LIMITED, GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE), and the parts of the other source are still filled. Failures are written to the Log section by the views' own code, and update `sources` at once.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: True skips the saved copies of the website list, the domains and the deploys and asks Hostinger again (counts towards the 50 requests per minute); the Git connections keep their five-minute copies

get.summary: The user's Hostinger websites (from Hostinger, or the copy saved in the last 60 s)
get.description: Follows all pages of Hostinger's website list. Hostinger's answers are kept in memory for 60 seconds and reused, so `fetchedAt` may be up to a minute old; `refresh=true` asks Hostinger again. Dockline sends Hostinger at most 50 requests per minute across all features; a request over that waits its turn (up to a minute, then HOSTINGER_UNAVAILABLE). Errors are problem responses with a stable `code` property: HOSTINGER_NOT_CONNECTED (409), HOSTINGER_TOKEN_REJECTED (409, replace the token), HOSTINGER_RATE_LIMITED (429, Retry-After header when Hostinger sends one) and HOSTINGER_UNAVAILABLE (502). Hostinger failures are written to the Log section and update HOSTINGER in GET /api/status at once.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: True skips the copy saved in the last 60 seconds and asks Hostinger again (still counts towards the 50 requests per minute); the new answer is saved

409.description: code HOSTINGER_NOT_CONNECTED: no Hostinger token saved; code HOSTINGER_TOKEN_REJECTED: Hostinger rejected the saved token (revoked or expired), replace it

429.description: code HOSTINGER_RATE_LIMITED: Hostinger's rate limit is reached

502.description: code HOSTINGER_UNAVAILABLE: Hostinger could not be reached, timed out, failed or answered unexpectedly

get.description: Reads Hostinger's domain portfolio. Hostinger's answers are kept in memory for 60 seconds and reused, so `fetchedAt` may be up to a minute old; `refresh=true` asks Hostinger again. Dockline sends Hostinger at most 50 requests per minute across all features; a request over that waits its turn (up to a minute, then HOSTINGER_UNAVAILABLE). Errors are problem responses with a stable `code` property: HOSTINGER_NOT_CONNECTED (409), HOSTINGER_TOKEN_REJECTED (409, replace the token), HOSTINGER_RATE_LIMITED (429, Retry-After header and retryAfterSeconds) and HOSTINGER_UNAVAILABLE (502). Hostinger failures are written to the Log section and update HOSTINGER in GET /api/status at once.

get.summary: The user's repositories, fetched from GitHub now
get.description: Every call asks GitHub (no cache) and follows all pages. Errors are problem responses with a stable `code` property: GITHUB_NOT_CONNECTED (409), GITHUB_TOKEN_REJECTED (409, reconnect), GITHUB_RATE_LIMITED (429, Retry-After header when known) and GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE (502). GitHub failures are written to the Log section and update GITHUB in GET /api/status at once.

SiteRepoRequest.description: The repository to link a site to

repoFullName.description: GitHub full name, owner/name; surrounding whitespace is ignored

SiteDetail.description: One site and the GitHub repository linked to it

repo.description: The linked repository; null when source is NONE

hostingerChecked.description: False when Hostinger could not be asked whether the site is Git-connected (see problems): source is then MANUAL or NONE from the saved manual links alone

repoWarning.description: Set when GitHub says the linked repository is missing or not accessible; null when it is fine, when there is no repository, or when GitHub could not be asked (see problems)

problems.description: At most one entry per source that could not be asked; empty when both answered

SiteLinkSource.description: Where a site's repository link comes from. HOSTINGER: the site is Git-connected in Hostinger (hPanel's Git section or Git auto-deployment); this always wins and cannot be changed in Dockline. MANUAL: linked by the user in Dockline (saved in the settings file). NONE: no repository is linked.

SiteRepo.description: The GitHub repository linked to a site

SiteRepoWarning.description: The linked repository is missing or not accessible on GitHub; the link itself is kept

SiteRepoWarningCode.description: REPO_NOT_FOUND: GitHub does not know the repository (deleted, renamed away, or private and not visible to the connected GitHub user). REPO_NOT_ACCESSIBLE: GitHub refuses access to it. REPO_MOVED: it was renamed or transferred.

SiteSourceProblem.description: One source (Hostinger or GitHub) could not be asked; the rest of the answer is still valid

code.description: The same stable codes as the problem responses of the list endpoints: HOSTINGER_NOT_CONNECTED, HOSTINGER_TOKEN_REJECTED, HOSTINGER_RATE_LIMITED, HOSTINGER_UNAVAILABLE, GITHUB_NOT_CONNECTED, GITHUB_TOKEN_REJECTED, GITHUB_RATE_LIMITED, GITHUB_UNAVAILABLE

retryAfterSeconds.description: For the RATE_LIMITED codes: seconds to wait, when known; otherwise null

HostingerTokenRequest.description: A Hostinger API token created in hPanel

token.description: The API token; surrounding whitespace is ignored

ConnectionState.description: CONNECTED: a token is stored and works (green). LIMITED: works, but not fully, e.g. missing permissions or rate-limited (yellow). ERROR: a token is stored but cannot be used, e.g. revoked, or the token store is unavailable (red). NOT_CONNECTED: no token is stored (red).

message.description: Why the state is what it is (always for LIMITED and ERROR; may be set otherwise, e.g. 'Connected as octocat'); never contains a token

retryAfterSeconds.description: Only while the source asked Dockline to wait (LIMITED after a 429 with Retry-After): whole seconds left before Dockline asks it again, at least 1; null otherwise

GithubDeviceCode.description: Show userCode and open verificationUri; then poll every intervalSeconds

userCode.description: Short code the user types on GitHub's page

verificationUri.description: Page to open in the browser

intervalSeconds.description: Poll POST /api/github/connect/poll no more often than this

GithubConnectProgress.description: Result of checking whether the user has approved yet

intervalSeconds.description: For PENDING: seconds to wait before polling again (grows by 5 when GitHub asks Dockline to slow down)

message.description: For DENIED, EXPIRED and ERROR: what happened, for the user

GithubConnectState.description: NOT_STARTED: no connection attempt since the app started (or since disconnect). PENDING: waiting for the user to approve on GitHub; poll again after intervalSeconds. CONNECTED: approved; the token is saved. DENIED: the user clicked Cancel on GitHub; start again to retry. EXPIRED: the code expired before it was approved; start again to retry. ERROR: something else went wrong, see message; start again to retry.

UNKNOWN: there may be a deploy, but its status is not known: the source could not be asked (see the site's problems) or reported a state Dockline does not know. NONE: no deploy information exists for this site (it is not a Node.js website, or it was never built).

OverviewProblemKind.description: What needs attention. DEPLOY_FAILED: a site's latest deploy failed. DOMAIN_EXPIRED: a domain has expired (Hostinger says so, or its expiry date is past). SOURCE_NOT_CONNECTED: GitHub or Hostinger is not connected. SOURCE_FAILING: GitHub or Hostinger is connected but not working fully (rate limited, token rejected, unavailable).

items.description: SOURCE_* problems first (GitHub, then Hostinger), then DEPLOY_FAILED (newest first), DOMAIN_EXPIRED, DOMAIN_EXPIRING (earliest expiry first) and LINK_BROKEN (by domain)
